public_rationale: BenevolentAI reported on April 5, 2023 that BEN-2293 met its safety endpoint but missed its overall secondary efficacy endpoints [e1]. Rentosertib's 12-week trial completed follow-up in August 2024; results published June 3, 2025 reported treatment discontinuations related to liver toxicity or diarrhea but concluded that further investigation was warranted [e2, e3]. These records do not establish repeated cases of animal efficacy followed by human safety failure caused by inadequate biological understanding [e1, e2, e3]. Their limited candidate coverage also cannot rule out such failures elsewhere [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: The packet lacks candidate-level records establishing the complete claimed sequence and its biological cause.
The cited trials do not establish long-term safety or provide a comprehensive accounting of AI-discovered drug failures.
Several potentially relevant primary records were inaccessible.
The claim supplies no numerical threshold for recurrence or precise definition of AI involvement.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Over and over, drugs discovered with AI work in animal trials but are not safe enough in humans, because we just don't understand biology well enough.

statement.excerpt: Over and over we discover drugs with AI that work on trials in animals but not safely enough in humans; we just don’t understand biology well enough.

from_speaker: we just don’t understand biology well enough
our_interpretation: The claim concerns repeated failures across distinct AI-discovered drug candidates, not merely adverse events in several patients receiving one drug.
“Not safely enough” means human safety or tolerability prevented viable development or use at an effective dose. An efficacy failure or commercial cancellation does not suffice.
The final clause attributes these failures to inadequate biological understanding.
The statement describes cumulative experience through publication, without supplying a starting date.
The wording concerns AI drug discovery generally, although the surrounding essay discusses cancer.
criteria.support_condition: Multiple documented candidates show animal efficacy followed by human safety failure, with investigations supporting inadequate biological understanding as the cause.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A sufficiently complete account of relevant candidates and failure causes shows that the asserted recurring animal-efficacy-to-human-toxicity pattern did not occur, or that its claimed causal explanation is wrong. Individual successes alone do not disprove recurrence.

evidence.locator: Statement by Chief Scientific Officer Anne Phelan; preceding trial-results paragraphs
evidence.explanation: The disclosed Phase IIa results met the safety endpoint while missing the overall secondary efficacy endpoints. This is counterevidence to treating AI-related trial disappointment as synonymous with human toxicity, but one candidate cannot disprove recurring failures elsewhere.

The AI-discovered candidate had a favorable short-term trial conclusion, although the abstract also reports treatment discontinuations associated with liver toxicity or diarrhea. Neither a favorable conclusion nor individual adverse events establishes or refutes the claimed recurring development-failure pattern.
This dates the trial underlying e2 before Marcus's post. The release also identifies generative AI involvement in target identification and molecular design.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Primary records documenting multiple AI-discovered candidates with animal efficacy followed by human safety failures that prevented viable development or use, with investigations supporting the asserted biological cause; or a sufficiently complete candidate-level accounting showing that the recurring pattern did not occur or its causal explanation is wrong, through March 16, 2026.
